## Tours offering an optional visit to Ahu Akahanga

[Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/) is an archaeological area on the coast of Rapa Nui, or Easter Island, which belongs to Chile. Remains of an ancient settlement, stone platforms, and fallen moai survive here. The site helps visitors understand how ceremonial spaces connected with island community life.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} offering the opportunity to add Ahu Akahanga **as part of an optional island itinerary**. The visit should not be considered part of the basic 14 days in Peru, Bolivia, and mainland Chile. Even if you choose the “Easter Island” option, the exact list of stops must be agreed in the final excursion itinerary.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_velikij_tur_po_yuzhnoj_amerike}}

## What you can see at Ahu Akahanga

At this archaeological complex, visitors can examine an ahu stone platform, moai that remain lying on the ground, and traces of houses from an ancient village. Nearby are foundations of traditional *hare paenga* dwellings and stone hearths known as *umu pae*. Along the coast, you can see evidence of how successive generations organized ritual and residential space.

The fallen statues offer a very different experience from restored rows of standing moai. Visitors see a monument in a condition that itself bears witness to historical changes in island society. Exploring the arrangement of the platforms and village is more rewarding than judging the site solely by the height of its statues.

In local tradition, the Akahanga area is associated with Hotu Matu'a, the legendary first ruler. Historical legends deserve attention, but they should not be presented as archaeologically proven accounts of every event.

## Which itinerary allows you to add Ahu Akahanga?

The [“14-day Grand Tour of South America”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) connects Peru, Bolivia, and Chile. The main route passes through Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca, La Paz, the Uyuni Salt Flat, the Atacama, and [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

**Easter Island is not included in these 14 days.** A separate “Easter Island” itinerary lasting 3 days and 2 nights is available. It includes an introduction to Rapa Nui's archaeological monuments, including [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), and other sites.

Ahu Akahanga can be considered as an additional visit, but its inclusion must be agreed in the plan for the island excursions. This allows you to find out in advance whether there will be time to see both restored monuments and the fallen statues of the ancient settlement.

## How much does the optional island extension cost?

A **3-day Easter Island program** with accommodation in a 3-star hotel can be added to the 14-day tour for a separate charge. Per-person rates depend on room occupancy:

| Accommodation | Price per person |
|---|---:|
| SGL | $1 116 |
| DBL | $780 |
| TPL | $754 |

These prices apply to the entire island extension, **not to a separate entrance ticket for Ahu Akahanga**. Excursions and transfers are arranged for English-speaking groups. Private guiding and a Russian-speaking guide are available for an additional fee. Flights should also be checked separately against the commercial terms of the itinerary.

When selecting particular archaeological sites, consider the protected area's operating days, access rules, and the excursion's actual content. The existence of a 3-day program alone does not guarantee enough time to see every well-known monument on the island.

## Ahu Akahanga and other Rapa Nui platforms

Each archaeological site reveals a different story. [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is known for its long restored row of moai; [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is the quarry where many statues were made; and [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) has seven restored figures associated with the legend of early seafarers.

Ahu Akahanga reveals not only moai but also surviving traces of an ancient village. For travelers interested in the development of island society, it complements visits to the better-known monumental complexes.

| Site | Main interest |
|---|---|
| Ahu Akahanga | Remains of an ancient settlement |
| Ahu Tongariki | Restored moai |
| Rano Raraku | Statue production |

To avoid turning the excursion into a succession of brief photo stops, allow time for the guide's explanations and for understanding how the sites differ.

## Preparing for the visit

Rapa Nui archaeological sites are subject to national park rules. Platforms and statues are not ordinary scenery: their condition requires care, and access depends on designated paths and current regulations.

Because the site is exposed to wind, bring comfortable shoes, sun protection, and a light windbreaker. Photographs may be taken only from areas open to visitors. When selecting an excursion, ask in advance whether Ahu Akahanga can be combined with other monuments without rushing.

For more about the island, explore [places to visit in Chile](/chile/place/) and the [Chile tour catalog](/chile/tour/). Ada Tours can help arrange specific archaeological stops within the optional 3-day island extension.

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Akahanga

### Is Ahu Akahanga included in the main 14-day tour?

No. The main route covers mainland Peru, Bolivia, and Chile. Easter Island is an optional extension, and the exact route through its monuments is confirmed when that option is selected.

### What makes Ahu Akahanga different from restored platforms?

You can see fallen moai, stone platforms, and traces of dwellings. They help bring the ancient village and changes to its ceremonial structures to life.

### Is there a separate charge to visit Ahu Akahanga?

The published price covers the 3-day island program as a whole. Specific entrance-ticket and guiding requirements should be checked against the confirmed contents of the chosen excursion.

### How much time should I allow for Easter Island?

The optional extension to the tour provides 3 days and 2 nights. The duration of a particular Ahu Akahanga visit is not separately guaranteed in this description.

## Tours via Ahu Akahanga: choosing an Easter Island trip

[Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/) is an archaeological area on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), where stone platforms and fallen moai survive beside the ocean. A visit reveals a ceremonial monument in a very different state from the restored rows of standing statues.

When choosing your trip, the most important decision is how much time you want to spend on Rapa Nui itself. A short tour concentrates on the island, while a longer journey may also include the Atacama, Patagonia, and other South American countries.

## Which tours visit Ahu Akahanga?

[“Easter Island: Three Days among Moai and Volcanoes”](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) is a compact 3-day itinerary focused on Rapa Nui's archaeological and natural sites.

[“Colorful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island”](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/) lasts 6 days and combines [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) with the island's monuments. It suits travelers who want to explore both Chile's capital and Rapa Nui culture.

The [Best of Chile tour with Easter Island](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/) lasts 12 days. The island, the Atacama Desert, and Patagonia are all included in one journey, so archaeological stops occupy only part of the total time.

Ahu Akahanga also features on longer trips: the [17-day grand tour of Chile and Argentina with Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) and the [33-day VIP journey through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/). Choose these tours for the broader combination of countries and landscapes, rather than for a single archaeological site.

## What you experience at Ahu Akahanga

The fallen moai, stone foundations, and exposed coast are the main points of interest. Instead of an imposing row of restored statues, visitors see another chapter in the ceremonial complex's history. It is best understood in the wider context of how Rapa Nui monuments were created, moved, and preserved.

Sites with similar themes but different purposes include [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), where many moai were carved, and [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), known for its restored row of standing figures. [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) reveal other aspects of the island's stone sculpture. The list of sites provides only a general outline: the tour you choose determines the exact sequence.

[Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) offers another island landscape and a glimpse of its coastal environment. A beach stop, however, does not replace an archaeological excursion.

## Three days or a longer Chile itinerary?

If your main interest is moai and Rapa Nui culture, several full island days without numerous additional flights make sense. A [short island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) lets you focus on the principal monuments.

Combining the island with Santiago introduces you to more of [Chile](/chile/) beyond Rapa Nui. The 12-day itinerary also highlights contrasts on the mainland: the arid Atacama and the mountains and glaciers of Patagonia. The 17- and 33-day programs require additional consideration of international travel and more complex overall logistics.

Compare more than the total number of days: look at nights spent on the island, the order of archaeological visits, flying time, and the pace of the sightseeing program.

## How to visit Rapa Nui monuments

Ahu Akahanga is within Rapa Nui National Park. Its archaeological structures require careful treatment: visitors must not climb onto ahu platforms or moai, touch the statues, or remove stones. Stay on marked paths and follow the park authorities' instructions.

Check current access, guiding, and ticketing rules for your travel dates. On the island's exposed coastline, bring drinking water, comfortable shoes, and protection from sun, wind, and possible rain.

## Frequently asked questions about tours via Ahu Akahanga

### How is Ahu Akahanga different from Ahu Tongariki?

At Ahu Akahanga, fallen moai and the remains of platforms show a monument in a different state. [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is famous for its restored row of standing statues.

### Can I see the island's main monuments in 3 days?

There is a [3-day itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) for a first introduction, but the depth of each visit depends on the program and logistics.

### Can a tour including Ahu Akahanga also take me to Patagonia?

Yes. The [Chile tour catalog](/chile/tour/) includes itineraries combining the island with the Atacama and Patagonia. They require more time for mainland travel and flights.

lead: >-

## Ahu Akivi: seven moai away from the coast

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) is a ceremonial stone platform on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), where seven moai stand in one row. Against the open grassy landscape, the silhouettes, sequence, and proportions of the figures are easy to appreciate. Yet the complex's architectural importance goes beyond the number of statues.

Most well-known ahu lie closer to the coastline. Ahu Akivi is unusual because it is located inland. At the same time, its statues face toward the sea. Chile's Rapa Nui Museum notes this characteristic and a possible spatial connection with another archaeological site, Ahu Vaiteka.

For travelers, Ahu Akivi is a chance to see moai away from the familiar coastal backdrop. Historically, it is also the result of one of the island's most significant restorations.

## How and when Ahu Akivi was restored

According to the Rapa Nui Museum, restoration work at Ahu Akivi took place in **1960–1961**. It was the first monument on the island where moai were raised back onto a platform through a scientific archaeological restoration. Before the work, the figures did not appear as they do today.

The standing statues are therefore authentic monuments of island culture, but their present upright position is the result of modern restoration. During an excursion, it is worth discussing what archaeologists learned about the original structure through excavation and what the restoration has made visible to visitors.

At [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), a longer row of restored figures can now be seen. When comparing the sites, consider the number of statues, the scale of the platforms, their settings, and the different stages of archaeological research.

## Do the statues really represent seven scouts?

Ahu Akivi is associated with a legend about seven messengers sent to the island by the legendary ruler Hotu Matu'a before his own arrival. The seven figures have become a natural symbol of this story.

However, this is **a traditional legend, not a proven identification of seven specific individuals**. Museum sources describe it as a later explanation of the ensemble. A more reliable approach is to distinguish what is visible on the platform from the stories preserved in Rapa Nui oral tradition.

Similar caution is needed with popular claims that every detail of the moai's orientation can be explained by a precise astronomical purpose. Possible relationships with the sun's position are being studied, but the fact that the statues face the ocean does not by itself establish that the structure was an observatory.

## Other sites to visit on the same sightseeing day

Ahu Akivi fits well into a tour of archaeological sites in central Rapa Nui. [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) reveals the source of red volcanic rock used to make the pukao stone headpieces. [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) introduces ceremonial platforms in a different coastal setting.

At [Ahu Hanga Poukura](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/), fallen statues remain, so after Ahu Akivi visitors can see a monument before full restoration. To understand how the moai themselves were produced, consider adding [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), where many sculptures were carved from volcanic tuff.

It is better to build an itinerary around a few contrasting sites, allowing time for explanations and walking. Compare the island portions of our trips in the [Chile tour catalog](/chile/tour/), and check which of the monuments listed are actually included in the particular tour.

## Access and visiting rules

Ahu Akivi is a protected site within Rapa Nui National Park. An entrance ticket and an accredited guide are required. Visitors must not touch the statues or stone platform, or use them as close-up photo props; stay on designated paths and at authorized viewpoints.

The open landscape can bring wind, sun, and brief rain showers. Comfortable closed-toe shoes and a light jacket are appropriate. Check the exact visiting hours and current park rules before setting out.

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Akivi

### How many moai stand on the platform?

**Seven.** They form one row on the restored ceremonial ahu.

### Why is Ahu Akivi considered unusual?

The platform is located inland, yet its moai face toward the ocean. This composition is uncommon among the better-known coastal monuments.

### When were the seven moai restored?

The Rapa Nui Museum dates the scientific restoration to **1960–1961**.

### Do the seven statues represent Hotu Matu'a's seven scouts?

That is what local tradition says. There is no scientific proof that the sculptures depict those seven particular figures.

## Tours with the option to visit Ahu Akivi on Easter Island

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) is a ceremonial platform on Easter Island with **seven restored moai**. The stone figures stand in a row amid grassy hills. According to Rapa Nui tradition, they are associated with seven early seafarers who reached the island before the main group settled there.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} where Ahu Akivi can be visited by selecting **an optional Rapa Nui program**. It is not part of the mainland-country route and must be arranged separately. It would be a mistake to treat this stop as an included day in Santiago de Chile: the island lies far from the mainland in the Pacific Ocean.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_velikij_tur_po_yuzhnoj_amerike}}

## What makes the seven statues of Ahu Akivi special?

The defining feature is a row of seven moai on a single platform. These figures were restored in the 20th century, so today visitors can see the whole composition rather than just individual fallen sculptures. Their orientation relates to islanders' ideas about how sacred monuments were positioned in space.

Local oral tradition tells of seven scouts dispatched by the leader Hotu Matu'a. A guide can help connect these stories with the archaeological landscape without confusing legend with established dates of historical events.

Ahu Akivi is worth visiting alongside complexes where moai survive in different conditions. The fallen statues and traces of an ancient village at [Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/) tell one story, while Ahu Akivi's restored platform tells another.

## The main tour through Peru, Bolivia, and Chile

The [“14-day Grand Tour of South America”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) begins in Lima and continues through Cusco, Machu Picchu, and Lake Titicaca. Travelers then cross La Paz, the Uyuni Salt Flat, and Bolivia's high-altitude areas, heading to the Atacama Desert and [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

The main **14 days / 13 nights** focus on mainland attractions. Easter Island can be added as a separate **3-day / 2-night extension**. Neither the main tour's title nor Ahu Akivi's inclusion in the optional catalog means moai can be seen en route across the desert or during an ordinary sightseeing day in Santiago.

Once you choose the island extension, its itinerary can be arranged around the monuments most important to you. Ahu Akivi is specifically mentioned among the archaeological sites that can form part of this extension, alongside [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), and [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/).

## Price and guiding for the island extension

The optional island portion can be added to the main tour at separate rates, with accommodation in a 3-star hotel:

| Accommodation | Price per person |
|---|---:|
| SGL | $1 116 |
| DBL | $780 |
| TPL | $754 |

These are rates for the **3-day extension**, not for a standalone excursion to the seven moai. Transfers and excursions on the island are arranged for English-speaking groups. Private arrangements and a Russian-speaking guide are available separately for an additional fee.

When planning, check the specific island flights, sightseeing dates, and monument access rules. The duration of the island stay alone cannot guarantee visits to every famous ahu: the number of sites depends on the selected route.

## Which sites to combine with Ahu Akivi

To gain a fuller understanding of Rapa Nui culture, compare the meaning of different monuments rather than similar-looking photographs.

**[Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/)** is a volcanic quarry associated with moai production. **[Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/)** is known for its long restored platform with numerous statues. **[Puna Pau Quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/)** reveals how red stone *pukao* headpieces were made. **[Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/)** is a coastal ceremonial complex.

| Site | Main theme |
|---|---|
| Ahu Akivi | Seven restored moai |
| Rano Raraku | Statue quarry |
| Puna Pau | Red stone used for pukao |

Ahu Akivi is a good choice if you are particularly interested in island traditions and monument restoration. If time is short, it is better to select a few archaeological sites and explore them thoughtfully than to try to see the whole island in a few hours.

## How a visit to the island works

A visit to Rapa Nui usually starts in [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/), the island's main settlement. Excursion vehicles travel along roads to protected archaeological sites. Some areas can only be visited with an escort and in accordance with current park rules.

Ahu Akivi stands in open country. Comfortable shoes and protection from wind and sun are needed. Access to moai and platforms is limited to authorized routes, as the ancient structures are vulnerable to damage.

If you are planning several archaeological sites, discuss in advance with Ada Tours which ones are included in the island program, how sightseeing days are distributed, and whether the standard sequence needs to change.

## Who will enjoy this extension?

Ahu Akivi is particularly interesting for travelers who want to discover **Rapa Nui's living cultural memory** after exploring the heritage of the Andes. One long journey then connects the Inca monuments of Peru, the cultures of the Altiplano, and a very different Pacific island tradition.

The extension requires additional days, flights, and accommodation. If your primary interest is mainland South America, the core 14 days already cover an extensive range of destinations. If you dream of seeing the seven moai on Easter Island, it is worth setting aside a proper island stay.

To compare routes, see [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [culture and history travel themes](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Akivi

### Is Ahu Akivi part of the main 14-day tour?

No. The main journey covers Peru, Bolivia, and mainland Chile. Easter Island is offered as a separate 3-day, 2-night extension.

### Why are there seven moai at Ahu Akivi?

According to local tradition, the seven figures are linked to a legend about Rapa Nui's first scouts or seafarers. The historical interpretations and legends are best discussed with a guide.

### Can I visit Ahu Akivi and Ahu Akahanga on the same trip?

Both monuments are on the same island, but visiting them together depends on the excursion route. Check that both stops are included in your chosen itinerary.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide included in the island extension price?

The published terms provide for English-speaking group excursions. Private guiding and a Russian-speaking guide are available as separately paid services.

## Which tours visit Ahu Akivi?

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) is an inland Rapa Nui ceremonial platform with seven restored moai. Unlike most similar monuments, these statues face toward the ocean. According to local tradition, they are associated with seven scouts sent by Hotu Matu'a. The visit reveals a distinctive side of island culture, different from the famous rows of statues along the coast.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose main itineraries pass through Ahu Akivi. When choosing, consider not only the total length of the journey but also the number of days on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), the excursion format, and the timing of your return flight.

## From 3 days on the island to a trip with Santiago

The [3-day “Easter Island: Three Days among Moai and Volcanoes” tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) includes Ahu Akivi on its third-day excursion. Alongside its restored statues, travelers visit the unrestored [Ahu Hanga Poukura](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/), the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), and [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/). This is a good combination for understanding how the island's monuments differ within a short stay.

On the [“Colorful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island” itinerary](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/), the Ahu Akivi excursion follows time exploring Chile's capital, the coast, and other Rapa Nui sites. The island program includes a group trip with an English-speaking guide to Ahu Akivi, Hanga Poukura, Puna Pau, and Tahai, followed by the return to the mainland.

The [10-day private tour](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/) includes Santiago, Valparaíso, Viña del Mar, and the Maipo Valley. On the island, the itinerary features Ahu Akivi, [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), and [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). Compare the order of individual sightseeing days carefully, as much of the journey also covers mainland Chile.

## When to choose a longer journey

On the [12-day Chile itinerary](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/), Easter Island complements the Atacama and Patagonia. The Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau excursion becomes one stage in a journey through regions with very different landscapes.

Longer options include the [17-day Chile and Argentina grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) and the [33-day Peru, Bolivia and Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/). Both include Ahu Akivi in the main island excursion. These trips are chosen to visit multiple countries; if your main priority is Rapa Nui culture, a separate short itinerary allows more focus on archaeology.

## Why Puna Pau and Tahai are often visited with Ahu Akivi

At Ahu Akivi, you encounter the completed figures and their placement. [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) is associated with red stone extraction for the statues' *pukao* headpieces. [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) presents other ceremonial platforms. Together, the sites reveal several stages of history and different types of archaeological structures.

Another useful comparison is [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), with fifteen restored moai, and nearby [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), where statues were carved from volcanic rock. These are usually visited on a different day. Seeing all the names in an island description does not mean they are covered in one excursion.

## What to check before booking

Check whether Ahu Akivi is visited on the departure day: on the [3-day tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), the excursion comes before the airport transfer. Compare private and group arrangements, guide language, meals, and transfers for the specific itinerary. When planning, allow for a separate flight between Santiago and Easter Island and follow the current rules for archaeological sites.

## Frequently asked questions about routes through Ahu Akivi

### How does Ahu Akivi differ from Ahu Tongariki?

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) has seven moai in the island's interior; [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) has fifteen restored figures on the coast. Many trips visit both platforms on separate excursion days.

### Can I see Ahu Akivi in 3 days?

Yes. The [3-day program](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) includes it on the final day's excursion with Puna Pau, Hanga Poukura, and Tahai. The sightseeing schedule must fit the departure time.

### Should I choose a long tour just to see Ahu Akivi?

Not necessarily. A separate trip to Rapa Nui is enough to discover the moai. Longer itineraries are worthwhile if you also want to explore the Atacama, Patagonia, Peru, or Bolivia.
